newsitem.title: USA: Gore announces $112 million in rural water projects.
newsitem.headline: Gore announces $112 million in rural water projects.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore Friday announced $112.4 million in new grants and loans for safe drinking water projects, mostly in rural areas.

"It's hard to imagine but, even in 1997, millions of Americans raise their families without a resource as basic and as necessary as safe drinking water," Gore said in announcing the latest round of funding for safe drinking water projects.
The Agriculture Department estimates that 2.5 million rural Americans are affected by poor water quality and availability. That includes almost 1 million without running water at home.

Some 5.6 million Americans face other serious water problems, including undersized or poorly protected water sources, a lack of adequate facilities and antiquated distribution systems, the department says.

The latest round of funding will finance 84 projects in 43 states and Puerto Rico. Since 1994, the Agriculture Department has provided more than $1 billion in loans and grants for safe-drinking water projects in all 50 states.

At the top of the list was a reservoir and water treatment project in Kansas, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman's home state, which will receive a $6 million grant and a $4.6 million dollar loan. Gore's home state of Tennessee will receive about $6.8 million in grants and $3.7 million in loans for four separate projects.
